llm.summary: The skill appears intended for web data collection, but it handles powerful tokens and local command execution with too little endpoint validation and disclosure.

dimensions.detail: The stated purpose, bundled scripts, and documentation coherently implement browser-extension data collection through a cloud connector or local bridge for the listed platforms.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: The cloud and local base URLs are user-configurable while bearer/admin tokens are attached to requests, and bridge startup accepts a shell-interpreted command; these are broader than a tightly scoped collection workflow.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No hidden installer, dependency fetcher, or automatic startup hook was found; the package is a skill document plus helper scripts.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Using the user's normal Chrome environment and connector credentials is purpose-aligned for browser collection, but it can touch logged-in browsing contexts and privileged connector APIs.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill persists cloud tokens in a preferences file, auto-reads a local bridge admin token when available, and can start a background bridge process when explicitly requested.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: Review this skill before installing. Use it only if you trust the cloud service and connector, avoid custom base URLs unless you control them, treat cloud tokens as secrets, prefer environment variables or a secret store over persistent preferences, and do not pass --bridge-cmd values from untrusted sources.
llm.findings:
[SDI-2] unexpected: Launching a local bridge is related to the skill, but accepting an arbitrary --bridge-cmd/WEB_COLLECTION_BRIDGE_CMD and running it through bash -lc is an under-scoped local execution capability.
[SDI-2] expected: Local admin-token use is expected for connector administration, but auto-loading it from environment or ~/.meixi-connector and sending it to a configurable base URL creates review-worthy scope risk.
[SQP-2] expected: Bearer-token cloud dispatch is required for the cloud workflow, but the scripts allow custom base URLs without HTTPS or host allowlisting and provide limited warning around token handling.
[SQP-2] expected: Reusable preferences are disclosed, and displayed tokens are masked, but defaultCloudToken is still stored persistently in a local JSON preferences file.
[SQP-3] expected: Chinese recovery prompts match the Chinese skill metadata and are not evidence of malicious behavior; they are mainly a usability/localization issue.
[E1] expected: External transmission to the cloud connector is central to the skill, but sending Authorization headers to caller-selected endpoints is the material concern.
[suspicious.dangerous_exec] expected: The static scan's preflight exec finding mostly reflects calling bundled helper commands and fixed binary checks, so it is downgraded; the separate bridge-cmd shell execution remains a real concern.
[VirusTotal] expected: VirusTotal telemetry was clean and did not add a negative signal.
